about: Utilities of Kowloon Walled City (九龍城寨) for the model week, Mon 15 to Sun 21 December 1986. The systems are water, power, refuse, drains and toilets, fire, gas and fuel, post and others. The file gives facts with sources, counts and a daily schedule. It puts places on the units of the frozen structure ([b, k, u] as in data/room_uses.json). It also gives placement rules and visuals for the drawing code. It has no colours: the drawing code gives the colours. See docs/utilities.md.
key: A unit is [b, k, u]: building id (S.list), floor k (0 = G/F), unit id (phaseOf(k).plan.units); the key "b:k:u" of S.unitNode. Positions (xz) are in the scene frame (see placement.frame). basis of places: verified, likely, guess. basis of facts and schedule items: sourced or inferred.

facts.text: The Government gave safe drinking water from eight standpipes. Only one standpipe, on Tai Chang Street (大井街), was inside the City.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: safe drinking water was available from just eight Government stand-pipes, of which only this one, on Tai Chang Street, was within the City.

facts.text: In 1987 eight standpipes supplied up to 35,000 residents and hundreds of factories. Seven of them stood outside the perimeter.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: By 1987, just eight stand-pipes were in place to supply up to 35,000 residents and hundreds of factories. Only one of these was located within the City

facts.text: WSJ also gives one standpipe inside and seven on the perimeter.
facts.source: The Wall Street Journal, 'Kowloon Walled City' interactive (2014), life chapter
facts.quote: only one official government standpipe located inside the Walled City's boundaries, and seven on its perimeter

facts.text: The Government put the standpipes on the edge of the City, at Tung Tau Tsuen Road (東頭村道) and Tung Tsing Road (東正道). The source writes 東頭邨道.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 余秋婷, 【真．城寨英雄（二）】九龍城寨特產「握手樓」　跨一步即可逃生, 27 Aug 2016
facts.quote: 後來亦只在寨邊的東頭邨道、東正道等位置設街喉，解決食水問題。
facts.type: retrospective (2016, reporter's narration of Yip Tak-wai, 葉德偉)

facts.text: As a child in the 1960s, Ng Kam Mui (吳錦妹) fetched water from taps at either end of Tung Tau Tsuen Road and bathed there.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: I remember when we were small we had to fetch water from taps at either end of the street. We even had our baths there

facts.text: Albert Ng counts about seven public water stations.
facts.source: Beijing Visitor, 'Journey into the Soul of the Kowloon Walled City with Pastor Albert Ng' (Albert Ng Kam-po, 吳錦波)
facts.quote: the government had about seven public water stations so we could get some water from there

facts.text: Albert Ng's family went to the public water stations every day to drink and shower.
facts.source: Beijing Visitor, 'Journey into the Soul of the Kowloon Walled City with Pastor Albert Ng' (Albert Ng Kam-po, 吳錦波)
facts.quote: Every single day, we would have to go the public water stations so we could drink and shower.

facts.text: The first standpipe came in 1963.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The first stand-pipe was installed in 1963

facts.text: In 1964 residents paid labourers $12-15 a month to carry six buckets a day from the standpipes.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Residents were paying $12-15 a month for labourers to carry six buckets of water each day from the stand-pipes to their flats

facts.text: Mains water went inside the City only to some recognised charities.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Mains water was supplied inside the City to various recognised charities, but this was very much the exception not the rule.

facts.text: In 1987 the Government surveyors found 67 working wells of about 40 suppliers.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Government surveyors assessing compensation claims identified 67 working wells owned by some 40 suppliers.

facts.text: Over the years, up to 300 'scientific wells' were sunk. Many ran dry.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: up to 300 'scientific wells' – as they were described by City-dwellers – were said to have been sunk beneath the area, though many had long run dry from overuse.

facts.text: The recent wells went down as far as 100 m.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The more recent drillings had to reach as far as 100 metres below the surface

facts.text: The well diggers were mainly property owners. Some were former water carriers.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The new well diggers were mainly property owners who were able to drill on their own land; some were reputedly former water-carriers themselves.

facts.text: Pumps lifted the well water to tanks on the roofs. Pipes ran down from the tanks into the blocks and flats.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Water was first pumped up to rudimentary storage tanks on the City roofscape. From there, a twisted congestion of pipes ran downward again, branching into blocks and flats.

facts.text: Many pumps ran at set times, usually noon and midnight. Each run gave a few hours of supply.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: many pumps would only be turned on at set times – usually noon and midnight – to replenish the tanks. This would only give a few hours' supply

facts.text: Residents stored water in baths and buckets. About 20 people controlled the supply for the well owners.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: residents still had to store water in baths and buckets. About 20 people were employed to control the supply at various locations according to the well-owner's schedule.

facts.text: A well-water link cost up to several thousand dollars.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Installation of a well-water link could cost as much as several thousand dollars, depending on the height above and the distance from the well.

facts.text: By the late 1980s a household paid $50 to $70 a month for well water.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: By the late 1980s, monthly charges were anywhere between $50 and $70 per household.

facts.text: Most residents had a well-water link.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: the majority of City residents appear to have been linked up to receive well-water.

facts.text: The well water was not fit to drink or boil. People carried drinking water from the standpipes until the end.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: it was not even fit to boil. Drinking and cooking water still had to be carried from the stand-pipes, and a small workforce was engaged in this activity till the end.

facts.text: All through the day, residents and paid carriers filled containers at the Tai Chang Street standpipe and carried them up the stairs. Letters in [] are hidden in the binding.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: people – some ordinary residents and others paid wat[er] 'suppliers' – appeared throughout the day to [fill] plastic containers and buckets that then had [to] be carried home, often up many flights of sta[irs].

facts.text: People also washed clothes and bathed at the standpipe. A food factory thawed frozen eels under a tap there.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: But people also came here with their washing [or] to bathe.

facts.text: Food-factory workers came from time to time to connect their hose to the standpipe and fill a tank in the factory.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Every once in a while a worker would appear to attach his business's hosepipe and thereby replenish a storage tank back in the factory.

facts.text: A large bundle of hoses ran from the standpipe to the food factories round it.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: A man washes his hair beside a great cluster of hosepipes that led off to the many food factories which naturally congregated in the area.

facts.text: The photos show the standpipe. A galvanised pipe frame at about 0.9 m carries 3-4 brass taps. Beside it stands a rounded concrete cylinder (about 0.5-0.7 m wide, 0.9-1.1 m high) with one more tap. The floor is tiled, with a kerb. 30-60 hoses go up the wall.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.cite: pp106, 109, 110, 111 (photos); p337 (Sing Pao 1987 photo, probably the same place)
facts.quote: The public stand-pipe on Tai Chang Street served all manner of residential and comme[rcial] needs.
facts.type: photo (c.1987-92); sizes are my estimates from the photo

facts.text: A notice of the Urban Services Department (市政總署) is painted on the wall at the standpipe. It says that the water of this well is not fit to drink. Thus a well is at this corner, or the corner taps give well water.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: 此井水不適宜飲用 市政總署

facts.text: The wall at the standpipe also carries the large painted characters 興發 and a board of 和興傢俬公司.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: 興發 ... 和興傢俬公司

facts.text: The corner store at Lung Chun Back Road (龍津後街) and Tai Chang Street was a few yards from the standpipe. A person waits at the standpipe in the photo.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: just yards away from the one Government stand-pipe located within the City

facts.text: Families carrying drinking water from the standpipes up to high floors were an everyday sight.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: families hauling drinking water from one of the eight Government stand-pipes up to their apartments on distant upper floors were an everyday sight.

facts.text: Wong Wai Chung's wife carried water up 10 storeys every day, and paid gangsters who controlled the taps.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Every day, she had to carry water up those 10 storeys. She also had to put up with gangsters controlling the taps, paying them money every time she collected water.

facts.text: Heung Yin-king carried buckets from the public taps up four floors every day.
facts.source: The Travel Club, John Carney, 'Kowloon Walled City: life in the City of Darkness', 3 Jan 2015
facts.quote: hauling buckets of water from the public taps up four floors to the flat every day

facts.text: Lau Chun-fat drew water at a public tap for drinking and cooking.
facts.source: SCMP, Peace Chiu, Mary Ann Benitez and Cannix Yau, 'Rats were something else: 25 years on ...', 23 Mar 2018
facts.quote: We had to go to a nearby public tap to draw buckets of water for drinking and cooking

facts.text: People tapped the mains illegally outside the City, at Sai Tau Tsuen (西頭村) and the Mei Tung Estate (美東邨). The Triads ran this at first.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: there was some illegal tapping of mains water from outside the City, notably from the adjacent Sai Tau Tsuen and Mei Tung estates.

facts.text: Illegal mains water stayed an important source of drinking water until the end.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: the illegal tapping of mains water remained an important source of drinking water until the end.

facts.text: The largest (stolen) main ran under the Lung Heung café (濃香冰室).
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The largest main ran beneath the Lung Heung café. There were some people 'releasing' water there

facts.text: Some company offices took rent and water charges, so that the collectors did not go from flat to flat.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: they are just places where residents can pay their rent and water charges, so that the collectors don't have to chase all over the place.

facts.text: Well owners sometimes locked the main tap for days and then asked $300 from each unit for a 'repair'.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: lock the main tap and disappear for a few days, before confronting the residents of a block with the news that the pump had malfunctioned and that $300 would have to be collected from each unit to fix it.

facts.text: Some well owners stopped the water when they lost at the casinos of Macau.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Many of these well owners were habitual gamblers – when they lost at the casinos in Macau, they would just stop the water.

facts.text: Drinking water was led to special wells and to tanks on the roof, then by pipes to the main flats.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Arrangements were made to allow drinking water to be 'diverted' to special wells and tanks on the roof, and from there through pipes to all the main apartments.

facts.text: Some blocks had several connections and a 24-hour supply. Most blocks did not.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Some builders made several connections to ensure a 24-hour supply, but this is not the case in most blocks.

facts.text: Well water often looked like drain water.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The water that comes from the wells often looks like drain-water and is usually undrinkable

facts.text: Each well owner got $200,000 in compensation for the wells.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The people who 'released' water are now receiving $200,000 in compensation for their wells

facts.text: Chan Shing, one of about 70 private water suppliers, collected the monthly charges himself.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: One of the City's 70 or so private water suppliers, Chan Shing collected monthly charges personally from his customers, occasionally waiving them for the elderly

facts.text: The pump was usually under a floor panel. The supplier switched it on at various times to fill a large tank on the roof. The photo shows an open floor hatch of about 0.8 x 0.6 m in a tiled room. Under it are a pipe, a valve with a hand wheel and an elbow.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Usually concealed behind a floor panel, the pump would be switched on at various times to replenish a large storage tank on the roof.

facts.text: Residents paid on time. They were afraid of a water cut or of damage to their pipes.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Residents would generally pay on time for fear their water would be cut off or their pipes damaged.

facts.text: In 1980 a Triad leader forced a rise in the water price with a threat.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: we'll chop him up in front of the crowd.

facts.text: 67 wells alone did not give enough water for 33,000 people and 700 businesses (feature text).
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: it is unrealistic to assume that 33,000 people and 700 businesses could have been supplied by 67 ground wells alone.

facts.text: The last natural ground well (19th century) was in an alley off Tai Chang Street. The photo shows a round concrete well-head of about 1 m diameter and 0.5 m height, with buckets.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: the only remaining natural ground well in the Walled City by the late 1980s was located, appropriately enough, in an alley off Tai Chang (Big Well) Street.

facts.text: There were two big wells. One was still in use. A building covered the other.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: There used to be two big wells in the City, but only one is still in use. The other has been covered over and a building has been erected on the site.

facts.text: Chan Pui Yin liked his well water. A friend from outside came for a pailful every day.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We use water from a well, which is good and has a pleasant flavour.

facts.text: Folklore: the well on the east side was filled in.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: this came about when a well on the east side of the City was filled in.

facts.text: The big well is beside 興發樓, No. 8 Tai Chang Street. People reach it from Lung Chun Road (龍津道) through two buildings.
facts.source: lichokiu.blogspot.com, 你早, 24 Sep 2005, citing 魯金《九龍城寨史話》(1988) pp132-133
facts.quote: 大水井在八號興發樓旁，從龍津道穿過祥興樓與兩合樓就可見到。

facts.text: Jetly Chau (周秀儀) fitted a meter and connected her shop to one of several well-water tanks.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: There are several well-water tanks in the Walled City and we installed a meter and connected our premises to one of them.

facts.text: Some families carried standpipe water for tea. Her shop paid a flat $100 a month for water.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Some of the families who do not like the brackish taste of well-water carry water from the nearby stand-pipes to make tea. The water here costs $100 a month, no matter how much we use.

facts.text: Chung Yuk Yee bathed her children in water from a roof tank fed by ground wells.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: bathing her son and daughter in the murky water piped from a rooftop storage tank fed by ground wells beneath the City.

facts.text: Chung Yuk Yee: the supply became slower and dirtier.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The water supply has definitely got worse; it's slow and there are black grains in the water that stain the clothes when they are washed.

facts.text: 林羅平: two owners held the power and the water supply as a monopoly.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 吳美松, 「九龍城寨︱德興魚蛋老闆城寨起家躍升行業龍頭　見證山寨工場沒落」, 20 Jul 2024 (reporter's narration of 林羅平)
facts.quote: 平哥指當時城寨內有兩戶業主，一人專門供電，另一人專門供水，不論供電還是供水，都是他們的專利。

facts.text: Staff of the Water Supplies Department (水務署; the source writes 水務局) came in from time to time and cut illegal pipes.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 吳美松, 「九龍城寨︱德興魚蛋老闆城寨起家躍升行業龍頭　見證山寨工場沒落」, 20 Jul 2024 (reporter's narration of 林羅平)
facts.quote: 那段日子不時有水務局人員進入城寨，並剪去一些偷水用的違法水喉

facts.text: Water came by time slots: 2/F-3/F at about 6-7 am, then 3/F-4/F at about 8-9 am.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 吳美松, 「九龍城寨︱德興魚蛋老闆城寨起家躍升行業龍頭　見證山寨工場沒落」, 20 Jul 2024 (reporter's narration of 林羅平)
facts.quote: 城寨居民用水要分時段，譬如二、三樓可能於早上6、7點來水，然後8、9時就輪到三、四樓有水用。

facts.text: A flat fee, not by meter: $100 a month for a home, $300 for a workshop.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 吳美松, 「九龍城寨︱德興魚蛋老闆城寨起家躍升行業龍頭　見證山寨工場沒落」, 20 Jul 2024 (reporter's narration of 林羅平)
facts.quote: 不按水錶收費，譬如住宅用戶每月繳交100元，開工場則每個月支付300元水費。

facts.text: 袁家倫 (13/F, top floor): water came only from 3 pm each day.
facts.source: 大紀元時報（香港）, 袁家倫, 【紀載香港】九龍城寨飛出的「火鳳凰」, 5 May 2024
facts.quote: 這裡每天下午三點鐘才有水供應
facts.date: years not given (she left Hong Kong in 1992)

facts.text: 袁家倫 took water from the roof tank with a small bucket.
facts.source: 大紀元時報（香港）, 袁家倫, 【紀載香港】九龍城寨飛出的「火鳳凰」, 5 May 2024
facts.quote: 也可以用小水桶到水箱打水用，不受制水的限制。

facts.text: Albert Ng: the well water came half an hour a week.
facts.source: Beijing Visitor, 'Journey into the Soul of the Kowloon Walled City with Pastor Albert Ng' (Albert Ng Kam-po, 吳錦波)
facts.quote: they dug into the ground and had underground water but the supply was half an hour per week

facts.text: 阿榮 (childhood, before 1986): the scientific wells gave water only a few hours each afternoon. Families filled large plastic buckets.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 麥佩雯, 「【真城寨英雄】 福利會才是黃賭毒大佬！　居民：說起來嚇怕女兒」, 28 Aug 2016 (阿榮)
facts.quote: 但每天只有下午數小時有供水；家家戶戶就在這幾小時長開水喉，用大膠桶裝滿一桶又一桶的貯水備用。

facts.text: 阿榮: the wells had no pressure. Only low floors got water. High floors carried water up from the ground.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 麥佩雯, 「【真城寨英雄】 福利會才是黃賭毒大佬！　居民：說起來嚇怕女兒」, 28 Aug 2016 (阿榮)
facts.quote: 「但科學井沒有水壓的，常常只有低層住戶才裝到水，高層的可能要去地面打水擔上樓。」

facts.text: Tam Sau-kuen (譚秀娟): no 24-hour water. At the sound of dripping water, even at night, she woke up to do the washing.
facts.source: The Wall Street Journal, 'Kowloon Walled City' interactive (2014), people and life chapters
facts.quote: There was no 24-hour water supply in Kowloon Walled City… No matter what time it was, even while we were sleeping at night, when we heard the sound of water dripping, we would immediately wake up

facts.text: Gordon Jones, former District Officer: about 70 wells; the water was very poor.
facts.source: The Wall Street Journal, 'Kowloon Walled City' interactive (2014), life chapter
facts.quote: The water was largely derived from about 70 or so wells, which the inhabitants of the Walled City had sunk… The actual quality of the water was pretty appalling.

facts.text: 陳先生 (a tall building on the edge of the City, no lift) paid $50 a month extra for water. He heard that private contractors held the water meters.
facts.source: 香港文匯報 (Wen Wei Po), 朱慧怡, 市民旅客看城寨電影場景, 7 Oct 2024 (陳先生)
facts.quote: 惟水費每月另外需要交50元，據說是城寨內的水錶是由私人承包。

facts.text: Chan So-hing's mother gutted fish at the street pump. The water was cold.
facts.source: SCMP, 'How a Hong Kong fish ball maker from Kowloon Walled City became a thriving family business', as copied by the firm (Chan So-hing, 陳素卿)
facts.quote: My mother would gut and clean all the fish by the pump, and the water was cold.

facts.text: 1974: residents brought water from municipal standpipes outside the City.
facts.source: UK House of Lords, HL Deb 11 June 1974, vol 352, 'Walled City of Kowloon'
facts.quote: brought from municipal standpipes outside the Walled City

facts.text: 1974: illegal wells were dug under the houses.
facts.source: UK House of Lords, HL Deb 11 June 1974, vol 352, 'Walled City of Kowloon'
facts.quote: illegal wells dug directly under the houses

facts.text: Early years: no supply. Young men carried water for weak old people at 50 cents a load.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 余秋婷, 【真．城寨英雄（二）】九龍城寨特產「握手樓」　跨一步即可逃生, 27 Aug 2016
facts.quote: 年輕人會以5毛一擔水作招徠，經營一盤小生意。

facts.text: Pipes broke and nobody repaired them: people added a new pipe. TV aerial cables, telephone lines and plastic water pipes filled the lanes.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 余秋婷, 【真．城寨英雄（二）】九龍城寨特產「握手樓」　跨一步即可逃生, 27 Aug 2016
facts.quote: 不過寨內街道上都是線，有電視天線、電話線等，亦有膠水喉，斷了不會修，只會再駁一條新的，互相交織

facts.text: 劉先生: rats, dirty water on the ground, leaking pipes, dripping in the humid spring.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 余秋婷, 【真．城寨英雄】 series (3 parts), 26-28 Aug 2016, as copied in primary-sources/hk01-kaifong-series-2016/SOURCE.md

facts.text: Girard: wires ran from building to building; water pipes overhead dripped.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 8 May 2024, interview with Greg Girard and Ian Lambot (2019), as copied in primary-sources/retrospective-testimony-web/SOURCE.md
facts.quote: 電線從一座大廈接到另一座大廈，頭上掛着水管，有水滴漏出

facts.quote: 10 to 15-story tenements, all without elevators, fire escapes or running water

facts.text: The City had more than 8000 households at its peak.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 余秋婷, 【真．城寨英雄（二）】九龍城寨特產「握手樓」　跨一步即可逃生, 27 Aug 2016
facts.quote: 最高峰時住了8000多戶

facts.text: Yim Kwok Yuen's workshop rent included electricity and water.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The rent for the workshop is $2000 a month, with electricity and water charges included.

facts.text: China Light and Power (中華電力有限公司) supplied the City in a major way from 1977.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: China Electric [now China Light and Power] began supplying electricity to the Walled City in a major way in 1977.

facts.text: Before 1977 only a few places on the edge had official supply: three supply points on Tung Tau Tsuen Road and 'United Road'.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: there were three supply points on Tung Tau Village Road and United Road.

facts.text: From 1977 CLP supplied legal buildings.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: by 1977, China Electric had come round to the idea of supplying electricity as long as the buildings were legal.

facts.text: 1977 was the year of the big fire. It started the change.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: That was the year of the big fire, when everyone realised things had to change.

facts.text: 1977-85: drastic change.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The years 1977 to '85 were years of drastic transformation.

facts.text: Before the master plan, about 20% of households had some supply, often illegal.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: before we drew up our master plan about 20 per cent of households already had some sort of supply – sometimes legal though often not.

facts.text: The City was a maze of pipes and wires.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The City was just a maze of pipes and wires all over the place.

facts.text: CLP brought the cable in from the outside, step by step.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Eventually we decided that we'd just have to make a start from the outside and work in – take the cable and enter inch by inch.

facts.text: Rock stopped the digging, thus CLP raised the pavement over the cable.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: we'd often strike rock or stone and have to stop. After several meetings in the City, we agreed to raise the level of the pavement instead!

facts.text: Sometimes CLP supplied a lower floor and the owner connected the floor above.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: In a few instances, we just supplied electricity to the power points on a lower floor and let the owner connect it to the floor above.

facts.text: CLP rented about 250 sq ft (about 23 m2) from the church in the City for a transformer.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We finally managed to persuade the church in the City to rent us around 250 square feet on condition we renovated their school.

facts.text: The transformer served two high-density cables.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: we had to find space for the transformer we needed to cope with two high-density cables we were planning to bring in.

facts.text: CLP built 'a couple' more substations on sites cleared by fires.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: release space cleared because of fires so we could build a couple more sub-stations.

facts.text: Permission came in 1984. The stations took three years.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: they eventually gave us permission in 1984. It took us three years to set up the stations

facts.text: By then almost every flat had electricity, but not all factories.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: By this time almost every flat had electricity. But that didn't take care of all the factories.

facts.text: Electricity thieves were only disconnected.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: They stole from China Electric but were rarely brought to account. If they were discovered, they'd just be disconnected.

facts.text: Wiring spread from a bank of meters on G/F to the flats above, tacked to the walls.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: a tangle of wiring spreads out from a bank of meters on the ground floor towards individual apartments on the floors above, the wires tacked directly to the walls.

facts.text: Meter readers carried torches and dog repellent. They read 400 to 5.. meters a day. In the scan, a smear hides the last two digits of the upper number; '500' fits the shape.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: the meter [read]ers – who were armed with torches [and] dog repellent – could cover 400 to 5[..] meters a day.

facts.text: The photos show three meter boards. On p98, a wall of meters and fuse boxes (about 3 x 1.5 m) is at a stair landing. Loops of flex and cables in conduit hang there. On p99, a board about 6 m long at 1.8-2.4 m in a G/F alley holds two rows of about 40 meters. On p101, a board about 1.2 x 1 m at a stair entrance holds about 20 meters.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The haphazard appearance of the [elec]tricity metering belied a certain [order].
facts.type: photo (c.1987-92); sizes are my estimates from the photo

facts.text: A CLP bill went to a G/F flat at 31 Lo Yan Street (老人街).
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: CHINA LIGHT & POWER COMPANY, LIMITED 中華電力有限公司

facts.text: Chan Kwong's factory cabling cost more than $30,000.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Look at this electric cabling – the installation of that alone cost more than $30,000.

facts.text: Inside the City the wiring was a mess, and houses shared one cable.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: That is not always the situation further inside the City. There, the wiring is often a mess and the power supply is affected by houses sharing the same cable.

facts.text: 'Poor electricity companies' stole power for factories at a low price.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: They used to steal electricity from the mains for people living in the City – factories and so on would pay a bill of only a few hundred dollars a month, when their consumption actually amounted to $1000 or more.

facts.text: Lam Shu Chuen (林樹全) rented out kerosene lamps in the 1940s, then sold power from generators, by the number of lights.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: I made my money in the 1940s by renting out kerosene lamps. Later, I provided electricity using generators. I charged according to the number of lights.

facts.text: Ng Kam Mui: no electricity in the 1950s and 1960s; kerosene lamps; later supply from CLP.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We eventually got electricity from China Electric; in the '50s and '60s there was none at all, so there were no fans or lights. We used kerosene lamps to study by

facts.text: Power cuts were frequent. The postman escorted people up the stairs with a torch.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The Walled City was often hit by power cuts, when the whole place would be plunged into darkness. I would take out a torch, and escort the children and elderly

facts.text: The Kai Fong Association (九龍城寨街坊福利會) paid for more than 200 public lights, on 24 hours a day.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We are now responsible for more than 200 lights which are switched on 24 hours a day, all paid for by the Association.

facts.text: The District Boards relaid some streets and put in some public lights.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: they have relaid some streets and installed some public lights for us.

facts.text: Many small alleys in the middle had light only here and there.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: many of the smaller alleys in the middle of the City were only intermittently lit.

facts.text: Tungsten bulbs in the flats; fluorescent tubes in the corridors.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 8 May 2024, interview with Greg Girard and Ian Lambot (2019), as copied in primary-sources/retrospective-testimony-web/SOURCE.md
facts.quote: 單位裏的鎢絲燈、走廊的光管

facts.text: 1987: low ceilings of wires, cables, fuses and sockets at head height.
facts.source: Gerald Posner, blog post of 26 May 2016, quoting his book Warlords of Crime (1988), visit of 1987
facts.quote: a bewildering jumble of knotted wires, dangling electric cables, and exposed fuses and sockets, all hanging less than a foot from the tallest cop's head

facts.text: 1987: an occasional bare bulb.
facts.source: Gerald Posner, blog post of 26 May 2016, quoting his book Warlords of Crime (1988), visit of 1987
facts.quote: an occasional naked bulb providing the barest light

facts.text: Albert Ng: the power company ran a wire in; the family had a meter and paid every month.
facts.source: Beijing Visitor, 'Journey into the Soul of the Kowloon Walled City with Pastor Albert Ng' (Albert Ng Kam-po, 吳錦波)
facts.quote: The electricity company would have a wire in and we would have a meter and we would pay every month.

facts.text: Wong Chan Pui-wah (黃陳佩華) paid somebody to steal electricity.
facts.source: The Wall Street Journal, 'Kowloon Walled City' interactive (2014), life chapter
facts.quote: We had to pay somebody to 'steal' electricity for us.

facts.text: The Kai Fong Association asked the power company to fit meters in each unit and helped run the cables.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 余秋婷, 【真．城寨英雄（二）】九龍城寨特產「握手樓」　跨一步即可逃生, 27 Aug 2016
facts.quote: 街坊福利會與電力公司聯繫，之後到每個單位安裝電錶，亦幫忙拉線

facts.text: 林羅平's shop had its own CLP meter because it was near the outer street.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 吳美松, 「九龍城寨︱德興魚蛋老闆城寨起家躍升行業龍頭　見證山寨工場沒落」, 20 Jul 2024 (reporter's narration of 林羅平)
facts.quote: 由於平哥的舖位近外街，因此他有一個電力公司提供的電錶及供電。

facts.text: Neighbours lent power: if the flat above lost power, it dropped a plug down.
facts.source: 明周文化 (Ming Pao Weekly), 梁伊琪, 【九龍城寨】黑暗之外 城寨人真實記憶, 13 Jun 2024 (平哥, 林羅平)
facts.cite: https://www.mpweekly.com/culture/社會/黑暗之城-九龍城寨-城寨居民-239629
facts.quote: 譬如樓上突然間沒有電，便扔個插頭下來，我們就借電給他用。

facts.text: 阿榮 (before 1986): each family connected itself; one wire for more than ten households; fires every night.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 麥佩雯, 「【真城寨英雄】 福利會才是黃賭毒大佬！　居民：說起來嚇怕女兒」, 28 Aug 2016 (阿榮)

facts.text: 1974: power was stolen from the mains outside by illegal connections.

facts.quote: stolen from the municipal mains supply outside the city by illegal connections

facts.text: 1987: buzzing electrical wires and dripping pipes, day and night.
facts.source: SCMP, Peace Chiu, Mary Ann Benitez and Cannix Yau, 'Rats were something else: 25 years on ...', 23 Mar 2018
facts.quote: Night and day within the Walled City were the same, with buzzing electrical wires, dripping pipes

facts.text: The Urban Services Department (市政總署, USD) collected the refuse: two tons a day.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: One essential service, however, was provided by the Urban Services Department (USD) refuse collectors. Clearing away the two tons of rubbish that accumulated each day in the City was a priority

facts.text: Refuse was also a fire hazard and fed the rats.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: control the large rat population – but equally to expunge the City of a potential fire hazard.

facts.text: USD buckets were everywhere. Many refuse collection points served 10 sweepers.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Orange USD buckets were commonplace, and numerous refuse collection points rationalised the cleaning system for the 10 sweepers who patrolled the City.

facts.text: Every year the Kai Fong Association ran clean-ups of roofs, alleys, pipes and cables.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: communal clean-ups of the rooftops, alleys and overhead piping or electricity cables that were organised every year by the Kai Fong Association.

facts.text: Photo p104: a bay of about 2 x 1.2 m in a covered alley about 1 m wide. It holds a low wooden bin (about 0.6 m high) full of plastic bags, and a broom. facts.quote: Refuse Collection

facts.text: The refuse collectors came at about 4 am on Tai Chang Street, with a lot of noise.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.cite: p93 (Lee Pui Yuen, 李培元, 12 Tai Chang Street)
facts.quote: the nights are pretty quiet until about 4am, but then the rubbish collectors come round crashing and banging.

facts.text: The KFA and the USD worked together on cleaning at Chinese New Year and on garbage.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We liaise over cleaning up during Chinese New Year and over the clearance of garbage.

facts.text: Only two buildings had lifts, thus garbage removal was hard.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Only two buildings in the City have lifts, so you can imagine how difficult it is to remove all the garbage from every apartment and factory.

facts.text: The KFA asked residents to take their garbage to the refuse collection station before work. Few did.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We have asked the residents to take their garbage to the refuse collection station before they go to work, but that is a bit unrealistic

facts.text: The KFA put up notices and posters about garbage.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Our publicity includes putting up notices and posters about garbage

facts.text: The KFA cleaned alleys, cleared drains, removed garbage and kept the main streets.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: During the last 20 years we have focused more on cleaning the alleys, clearing the drains, removing garbage and maintaining the main streets.

facts.text: A metal grill over the Tin Hau Temple (天后廟) caught the refuse thrown from the flats round it.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: the metal grill protecting it from all manner of refuse dispatched from the surrounding apartments

facts.text: The grill was cleared once a year. The photo shows a steel mesh (about 5 cm squares) over a light well about 6-8 m wide, at about 2/F. The refuse on it is 0.3-0.5 m deep.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: the protective mesh grill, which was cleared just once a year

facts.text: WSJ: garbage on the grate kept the sun off the Tin Hau Temple.
facts.source: The Wall Street Journal, 'Kowloon Walled City' interactive (2014), life chapter
facts.quote: was often blocked from sunshine by the garbage residents scattered on the tin grate above it

facts.text: Rubbish and plastic bags often filled the gaps between buildings.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Natural light penetrated to street level only in those few places where narrow gaps had been left between buildings, though all too often these were obstructed by plastic bags and assorted rubbish.

facts.quote: シャワールーム兼用と思われる。

facts.text: Residents in the stairways watched for fire.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: the residents were more acutely aware of – and vigilant against – the ever-present threat of fire.

facts.text: 1953 or 1954: a fire burned more than 3000 huts. It started at a rice and charcoal shop.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Then there was a big fire around 1953 or '54, when more than 3000 huts were destroyed. It started at a shop that sold rice and charcoal.

facts.text: The KFA night patrol (11 pm to dawn) watched for fires. It stopped in the 1970s.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: It would patrol from 11pm until dawn as a deterrent to thieves and helped as a lookout for fires. Both the time-reporting and fire-prevention teams operated on a voluntary basis and were discontinued in the 1970s.

facts.text: The KFA bought some fire-fighting equipment.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We bought some fire-fighting equipment.

facts.text: The KFA put up notices on fire prevention.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We do the same regarding fire prevention.

facts.text: Chung Yuk Yee feared the alley wiring: people blamed it for fires.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: I worry about the electric wiring in the alleys too – there have been fires in the City before and the poor wiring is always blamed.

facts.text: Fire engines did not get in. Inside there was a fire trolley with sand and buckets of water, and there were patrol teams.
facts.source: The Funambulist, Sharon Lam and her father, 9 Mar 2018
facts.quote: inside, there's fire prevention stuff, such as a make-shift fire trolley with sand & buckets of water. There were self-organized patrol teams.

facts.text: A rattan shop fire: a family on 6/F went down to 3/F and stepped across to the next building.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 余秋婷, 【真．城寨英雄（二）】九龍城寨特產「握手樓」　跨一步即可逃生, 27 Aug 2016
facts.quote: 樓下籐器店火災，劉先生一家人居於六樓，後樓梯被鎖，而三樓則對正旁邊大樓的走廊

facts.text: 阿榮 (before 1986): people beat gongs at midnight and shouted 'fire'.
facts.source: HK01 (香港01), 麥佩雯, 「【真城寨英雄】 福利會才是黃賭毒大佬！　居民：說起來嚇怕女兒」, 28 Aug 2016 (阿榮)
facts.quote: 經常睡到半夜就有人打鑼打鼓大叫「火燭呀」，要逃生。

facts.text: A toy factory had 4-5 wire fires each summer. Workers ran to the Tung Tau Tsuen Road entrance.
facts.source: Yahoo新聞 (Yahoo News HK), 鄭美姿, 九龍城寨小學有人未遺忘　城外人分享衝進去回憶：細細個入去做暑期工, 3 Jun 2024 (阿平)
facts.cite: https://hk.news.yahoo.com/ (article of 3 Jun 2024; full URL in data/people.json, id toy-factory-summer-boy)
facts.quote: 阿平最記得一個暑期工下來，總會發生四、五次「燒電線」事件

facts.text: Gordon Jones: no significant fires.
facts.source: The Wall Street Journal, 'Kowloon Walled City' interactive (2014), life chapter
facts.quote: there were no significant fires or outbreaks of disease

facts.text: 1974: fire risk was very high.
facts.source: UK House of Lords, HL Deb 11 June 1974, vol 352, 'Walled City of Kowloon'
facts.quote: Fire risk, because of the maze-like layout of the Walled City is, of course, very high.

facts.text: 1964: four emergency hydrants were removed after the drought.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Four emergency hydrants had been removed following the end of the drought that year, leaving just five stand-pipes.

facts.text: KFA poster: 'Prevent Fire: Protect Your Life and Property'.
facts.source: The Wall Street Journal, 'Kowloon Walled City' interactive (2014), life chapter
facts.quote: Prevent Fire: Protect Your Life and Property

facts.text: Every family used an LP gas cylinder. The KFA ran a safety campaign.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Every family here uses an LP gas cylinder, which is a bit like keeping a bomb in your home. If it exploded, the effect would be catastrophic and we have a campaign to encourage families to be careful.

facts.text: Lee Pui Yuen carried kerosene drums up 10 or more storeys.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: I could carry around 40 catties [60 pounds] of rice and a drum of kerosene up 10 or more storeys.

facts.text: His store opened 8 am to midnight; busiest 5-9 pm. It sold mainly rice, fuel and cigarettes.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We're open from 8am to midnight and the store used to be crowded between 5 and 9pm every day.

facts.text: GRS: Tak Sang LP Gas Hong (德生行), 9 Tung Tau Tsuen Road, G/F.
facts.source: Government Records Service (政府檔案處), catalogue HKRS1255-3 (clearance files)
facts.quote: Flat B, G/F, 9, TTT RD. [Tung Tau Tsuen Road], 2. G/F, Side Lane. (Tak Sang LP Gas Hong) 德生行

facts.text: 袁家倫: a shared kitchen, one kerosene stove per family; rice cookers in the rooms.
facts.source: 大紀元時報（香港）, 袁家倫, 【紀載香港】九龍城寨飛出的「火鳳凰」, 5 May 2024
facts.quote: 全屋共用一個廚房，每家只能放一個火水爐用來炒菜，電飯鍋就放在各人的房間。

facts.text: 1970s: a store sold LP gas in a 'huge can'.
facts.source: KowloonWalledCityBoy (Albert Ng), 'My Friend Ah Meng', 13 Oct 2016
facts.quote: that huge can of LPG gas

facts.text: The postmen worked from the Lung Kong Road Post Office in Kowloon City.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: I was working at the Lung Kong Road Post Office in Kowloon City.

facts.text: A sorting desk with 48 slots was too small for one day's mail of the City.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: A sorting desk with 48 slots was not enough to accommodate a day's mail for the Walled City.

facts.text: There were two postmen from 1982.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The number increased to two in 1982

facts.text: The round began at a store on Lo Yan Street, with deliveries to collective mail-banks.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Mr Lui's daily round began at a store on Lo Yan Street, from where he would embark on several separate sorties which took him to simple deliveries at collective mail-banks

facts.text: The postman crossed the roofs through skylights.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: On reaching a skylight, he would cross the rooftops

facts.text: Photo p145: many small wooden letterboxes (about 0.25-0.3 m) are fixed on both walls of a narrow alley at about 1.6-2.2 m. The postman sorts letters there. He wears a cloth hat. Photos pp102 and 148: single metal letterboxes of about 0.25 x 0.4 m at about 1.8 m.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Postman Lui Man Sang emerges from a building staircase and enters one of the Walled City's alleys while making his rounds.
facts.type: photo (c.1987-92); sizes are my estimates from the photo

facts.text: A postbox label: 94 Lung Chun Road, 5/F front.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: 龍津道94號 五樓前座

facts.text: Only two buildings had lifts.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: The Walled City only had two buildings with lifts.

facts.text: TV aerials on the roofs at the eye level of a child.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: Children at play on the roof of the Walled City, among television antennae precariously positioned at the eye level of a six year old.

facts.text: 袁家倫's building had no lift and no telephone.
facts.source: 大紀元時報（香港）, 袁家倫, 【紀載香港】九龍城寨飛出的「火鳳凰」, 5 May 2024
facts.quote: 可是卻沒有電梯，沒有電話

facts.text: Lam Po Chun was a postman in the City from 1979 to 1989.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: From 1979 to 1989 – that is, from my 19th to 29th year – I was a postman in the Walled City.

facts.text: Lam Po Chun says that the high-rise buildings had no lifts. On p146 he says that two buildings had lifts.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: there were no lifts in the high-rise buildings!

facts.text: Where roofs differed by one floor, people put a ladder. Where they differed by two or three floors, people opened or broke a corridor window of the taller building and put a stool under it.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: the residents would open or break a window in a lower corridor of the taller building, and put a stool under it so people could climb out on to the lower rooftop.

facts.text: Yim Kwok Yuen (嚴國源) thinks that half of his water is stolen from the mains and half comes from a well. He drinks mains water.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: I believe that half of the water is stolen from the mains, while the other half comes from the well. We all use well-water but we use water from the mains for drinking.

facts.text: Yim Kwok Yuen's workshop never had a power failure.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We have never had a power failure.

facts.text: His workshop has fans, a noisy refrigerator and a hot oven. His flat has an air-conditioner, a television and a washing machine.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: We have an air-conditioner, though we only use it on the hottest days; we also have a television and a washing machine.

facts.text: Photo p288 shows Yim Kwok Yuen's workshop. A metal LP gas cylinder stands by the stove. It is about 0.3 m wide and 0.6 m high, with a ring guard on the valve. Plastic buckets and a large steel basin are near it.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: A wide variety of cooked food, like these pigs about to be barbecued, was prepared within the Walled City
facts.type: photo (c.1987-92); sizes are my estimates from the photo

facts.text: Chu Yiu Shan (朱耀山): the standfirst of his interview calls him a property developer and estate agent.
facts.source: Greg Girard and Ian Lambot, City of Darkness Revisited (Watermark, 2014)
facts.quote: He operated as a property developer and estate agent for many years, only moving to Junk Bay when the clearance was announced.

meter_boards.rule: Put one board at each building with a G/F stair door (S.doors kind 'street', k 0): 226 boards. Fix it on the entrance wall beside that door, with the bottom edge at b.y[0] + 1.8 m. The number of meters m is the number of units of the building (all floors). The reason: the KFA had a meter fitted in each unit (U114). Total: 8352 meters.
meter_boards.layout: Put the meters in rows of up to 40, 0.15 m apart (p99). rows = ceil(m / 40), with at most 3 rows on one board. If m > 120, put a second board on the other side of the door. Board width = 0.15 x min(m, 40) + 0.3 m (fuse boxes). Height = 0.3 m for each row. Material: wooden board, small metal meters and fuse boxes.
meter_boards.cables: From the board, a bundle of flex goes up the stair shaft, tacked to the wall: one wire for each meter. At each landing, wires split off to the units of that floor (p100 caption). On named lanes, put a board with m of 40 or more on the lane wall outside the door (p99).
meter_boards.no_door: 51 buildings have no street door (no_door_ids). They get no board. Their meters are on the board of the building that gives them access (inferred).

overhead.named_lanes: Named lanes are the cells of S.L.streetLanes, about 634 m in all. Keys: kms Kwong Ming St (光明街), lys Lo Yan St (老人街), tcs Tai Chang St (大井街), skg Sz Kung St (社公街) and lsr Lung Shing Rd (龍城路). Also: abs Almshouse Back St, tts Tin Hau Temple St (天后廟街), lcb Lung Chun Back Rd (龍津後街) and tcn (north part of Tai Chang St). Over them, put a layer of 30-40 pipes and cables, 2.6-3.5 m above the lane floor, on wall brackets every 1.5-2 m.
overhead.other_lanes: Other lanes are the lane cells inside the City that are not named (S.L.alley 1, S.L.inside 1): about 4046 cells, about 2250 m. Over them, put 10-20 pipes and cables, 2.3-3 m above the lane floor. Where a building covers the lane, fix them to its ceiling.
overhead.vertical: On every facade that faces a lane: 2-6 pipes and cables down the wall from the roof to the G/F (photo pp114-115).
overhead.roofs: Between roofs: 1-4 cables strung at 2-4 m above the roof, and the tank pipes on the roof slab (pp322-323).
overhead.drips: On named lanes, put a drip sheet of plastic or metal under the overhead layer about every 6 m. Put it at 2.2-2.6 m, slanted to one wall (p249).
overhead.basis: inferred (density and heights from photos pp102, 105, 144, 322-323)

lamps.rule: These are the KFA public lights: more than 200, lit 24 h. Put one fluorescent tube every 8 m on the named lanes, on alternating walls at 2.5 m (84 lamps). Then put one every 20 m on the other lanes (about 120 lamps). More than 30 m from the City edge, leave one in four of the small-lane lamps dark (p103). On each stair landing, put one bare bulb or one tube.

refuse_points.rule: 23 points, one about every 32 m along each named lane (list). At each point: a wall recess bay with a low wooden bin (2 x 1.2 x 0.6 m) and 2-6 USD buckets. At the 10 points nearest a stair door, also a stack of 5-8 buckets.

letterboxes.rule: At each G/F stair door with m of 20 or more: 8-20 small wooden letterboxes on the entrance or alley wall at 1.6-2.2 m (p145). Elsewhere: 1-3 metal letterboxes beside the stair door at about 1.8 m (pp102, 148).

roof_refuse.rule: On each roof, put 1-3 heaps (about 2 x 2 x 0.4 m) of boards, plastic sheet and broken furniture. Put them against the parapet or the roof edge, away from the stair node.

gaps.rule: In each gap between buildings narrower than 1.5 m: rubbish 0.3-0.5 m deep at the bottom.
